economics.fiscal-assess-3.0001.all: Direct: progressive, raise large sums, fair; but disincentive to work (conflicts with aim), avoidance. Indirect: no direct work disincentive, hard to avoid, can target demerit goods; but regressive, raise prices/inflation. Judgement: indirect/mix fits aim, depends on equity concerns.

economics.fiscal-calc.0014.all: Direct = income tax + corporation tax = 27.2 + 9.8 = G£37.0bn

economics.fiscal-data.0013.b: Indirect taxes do not reduce reward from work, hard to evade, broad base, target demerit goods, raise revenue quickly.
economics.fiscal-data.0013.c: As assess-3: direct progressive but disincentive; indirect no work disincentive but regressive/inflationary; judgement.

economics.fiscal-define1.0006.all: The total amount of money the government owes from past borrowing (accumulated deficits).

economics.fiscal-define2.0006.all: The total accumulated debt owed by the government (1) built up from past budget deficits / borrowing (1).

economics.fiscal-describe.0013.all: A direct tax is levied on income/wealth and paid directly to government by the person (e.g. income tax) (1); an indirect tax is on spending on goods and services, collected via sellers (e.g. VAT) (1).

economics.fiscal-evaluate-1.0005.all: For: debt 102% high, interest costs, confidence. Against: cuts reduce AD/growth, unemployment, worse services, regressive sales tax, lower revenue. Judgement on timing/state of economy.

economics.fiscal-evaluate-2.0003.all: Benefits: jobs, growth, investment, lower pollution, competitiveness. Costs: opportunity cost of G£42bn, retaliation, inefficiency, time lag. Judgement.

economics.fiscal-evaluate-3.0003.all: As assess-3 for Kaleda with supported judgement.

economics.fiscal-explain.0014.all: Bonds let the council raise a large sum now (1) without raising local taxes, spreading cost over the life of the asset (1); funds the ₫79m public transport project immediately (1).

economics.fiscal-mcq-def.0007.all: Increasing government spending and/or cutting taxes to increase total demand

economics.fiscal-state-class.0003.all: Cutting income tax / increasing government spending

economics.globalisation-analyse-1.0005.all: More choice, lower prices from competition and economies of scale, better quality, access online; Porto stores; but slowing trade growth.

economics.globalisation-analyse-2.0003.all: Jobs, incomes, multiplier, tax revenue (after tax breaks), technology/skills transfer, exports, growth from O£948m investment.

economics.globalisation-analyse-3.0001.all: Low wages, poor conditions, exploitation, profits repatriated, dependence on MNCs (footloose), environmental damage, little skills transfer.

economics.globalisation-assess-1.0004.all: Benefits: choice, lower prices, quality. Against: domestic firms close/job losses, loss of culture, exchange-rate risk, unequal gains. Judgement.

economics.globalisation-assess-2.0006.all: For: attracts FDI M$1301m, jobs, technology, growth. Against: lost revenue, race to bottom, footloose MNCs, profits repatriated, unfair to domestic firms. Judgement.

economics.globalisation-assess-3.0006.all: For: 3m jobs, mainly women, incomes, exports. Against: low wages, conditions, dependence, profits leave. Judgement.

economics.globalisation-define1.0002.all: A firm that has its headquarters in one country and operates/produces in more than one country.

economics.globalisation-define2.0004.all: A country in which a multinational corporation sets up operations (1), that is not its home country where it is headquartered (1).

economics.globalisation-describe.0006.all: Profits are sent back to the home country (1) so less income stays in the host economy (1). (Or domestic firms forced out.)

economics.globalisation-evaluate-1.0002.all: As assess-1 for Oman with supported judgement.

economics.globalisation-evaluate-2.0003.all: As assess-2 for Zentara, Z£1389m, with judgement.

economics.globalisation-evaluate-3.0003.all: As assess-3 for Portugal, 1m jobs, with judgement.

economics.globalisation-explain.0005.all: Creates 3,000 jobs (1) so incomes rise, more spending and multiplier (1), reducing unemployment in Bangladesh (1).

economics.globalisation-analyse-3.0001.problem: Question asks for costs of producing for MNCs, but the indicative content lists only benefits (jobs, export earnings, incomes, skills).
economics.globalisation-analyse-3.0001.fix: Indicative content: low wages and poor conditions; dependence on footloose MNCs; profits repatriated to foreign owners; environmental damage; limited skills transfer, applied to Uganda's 4 million workers.
